pitfalls.what: Optional option-argument value is silently consumed as null when the next argv token looks like any option; --foo --bar produces foo=null, bar=true with no warning.
pitfalls.consequence: Users who miss a space or have a shell that re-tokenizes see a silent null and downstream TypeError far from the bug origin.

pitfalls.what: parseOptions only treats negative numbers as arguments when no ancestor has a matching numeric short flag (e.g. -1); the check walks every ancestor on every token.
pitfalls.consequence: Adding a short flag -1 anywhere in the command tree silently flips -1 from numeric argument to option, breaking downstream consumers; deep trees pay O(ancestors x options) per token.

pitfalls.what: -- literal-handling mutates behavior based on current dest: when dest=unknown, -- is pushed; when dest=operands, -- is dropped silently.
pitfalls.consequence: After an unknown option, -- stops acting as the everything-after-is-positional sentinel and positional args get silently reclassified.

pitfalls.what: Combo short flags -abc are processed char by char via activeGroup; if any middle char is not a registered option the leftover is reclassified (as operand with passThrough, or as unknown without).
pitfalls.consequence: Behavior diverges based on a flag users rarely set; non-deterministic-looking parse trees.

pitfalls.what: Option constructor decides required/optional purely by flags.includes('<') / flags.includes('['); any stray bracket flips the type silently.
pitfalls.consequence: Misformatted flag string (e.g. -x, --extra <type with no closing >) is treated as required; failures occur at parse time, not at registration.

pitfalls.what: Argument constructor switch on name[0] treats any name not starting with < or [ as required; name.slice(1,-1) is applied unconditionally.
pitfalls.consequence: argument('<thing') (missing closing >) yields empty _name; argument('<>') becomes a required empty-name argument that silently swallows any positional.

pitfalls.what: choices() overwrites this.parseArg with an internal closure; any prior .argParser() call is silently discarded.
pitfalls.consequence: argParser(parseInt).choices([...]) runs only the choices validator; non-string inputs bypass parseInt and fail with Allowed choices are... — no chaining.

pitfalls.what: _storeOptionsAsProperties (legacy mode) reads options from this[key]; user code that does program.foo = 42 silently corrupts the parsed value and defeats getOptionValueSource.
pitfalls.consequence: Legacy mode is no longer tamper-evident; buggy middleware makes getOptionValueSource lie about origin, defeating conflict detection and env-priority logic.

pitfalls.what: Deprecated APIs still wired in: _args (alias for registeredArguments), noHelp (alias for hidden), addHelpCommand 2nd-arg deprecated, RegExp arg-parser wrapped silently, outputHelp callback form, this.emit(--help).
pitfalls.consequence: Consumers relying on legacy names work but are on a slow-deprecation path; PRs touching those branches need deprecation comment in CHANGELOG and may want a runtime warning.

optional: Update JSDoc in lib/*.js (picked up by tsc -p tsconfig.js.json via checkJs)

exploration_log.observation: Created an honest gap-marked map to receive incremental audit evidence.

expert_domains.rationale: Option class is the largest dedicated module (lib/option.js ~580 lines), encapsulates flag-shape parsing (short/long/required/optional/variadic/mandatory), default/preset/choices/parseArg/conflicts/implies/env/DualOptions semantics, and is the high-stakes area where most parser bugs originate. ~20+ dedicated test files cover the surface.

key_files.purpose: Option class — flag parsing, defaults, presets, choices, conflicts, implies, env, parseArg, DualOptions

key_types.name: DualOptions
key_types.purpose: Pair of --foo / --no-foo options with preset-based source detection

patterns.name: flag-string-parsing
patterns.description: flags.includes('<') and flags.includes('[') decide required vs optional; /\w\.\.\.[>\]]$/ detects variadic; splitOptionFlags extracts short/long.

patterns.name: value-source-tracking
patterns.description: _optionValueSources records whether a value came from default, env, config, cli, or imputed (implied) — used for precedence and getOptionValueSource().

pitfalls.risk: flags.includes('<') / flags.includes('[') silently flip an option's required/optional type on any typo.
pitfalls.consequence: Misformatted flag strings (e.g. --extra <type with no closing >) become required; failures surface at parse time, not at registration.
If a custom preset on --no-foo matches --foo's default, getOptionValueSource('foo') returns 'default' instead of 'cli', defeating precedence logic.

conventions: One class per file; module filename matches primary export in lowercase/camelCase.
ESM only; relative imports carry .js suffix; node: prefix on built-ins.
Errors are CommanderError subclasses with exitCode/code/nestedError; user-facing errors include bulleted remediation hints after a newline.

expert_domains.rationale: Command class (lib/command.js ~2791 lines) is the orchestration hub: registration (option/argument/command), parsing pipeline (parseOptions/parseArgs), subcommand dispatch, executable subcommand lookup via childProcess.spawn, action handlers, lifecycle hooks, exit handling, configurable output, save/restoreStateBeforeParse. ~40+ dedicated test files.

key_files.purpose: Command class — registration, parse pipeline, subcommand dispatch, executable subcommands via childProcess.spawn, action handlers, lifecycle hooks, exit handling

key_types.name: Command
key_types.purpose: Public Command type — fluent builder, parse(), help, hooks, subcommands

key_types.name: HookEvent
key_types.purpose: Hook event id type for addHook('preAction'|'postAction'|...)

key_types.name: OptionValues
key_types.purpose: Parsed options container returned by opts()/optsWithGlobals()

patterns.name: copyInheritedSettings
patterns.description: Subcommand inherits output/help/exit/_storeOptionsAsProperties/_combineFlagAndOptionalValue/etc from parent on attachment.

patterns.name: factory-methods-for-extension
patterns.description: createCommand, createArgument, createOption, createHelp allow subclasses to swap implementation without overriding constructors.

patterns.name: EventEmitter-as-option-bus
patterns.description: addOption registers on('option:'+oname) and on('optionEnv:'+oname) listeners; parsing, env, and implied-option logic share one setOptionValueWithSource path.

patterns.name: parse-source-auto-detect
patterns.description: _prepareUserArgs picks argv source from process.versions?.electron (Electron), execArgv.includes('--print') (node --print), or process.argv slice — magic that is invisible to the caller.

pitfalls.risk: Silent null for optional option-argument when next token looks like an option (--foo --bar yields foo=null, bar=true).
pitfalls.consequence: Mis-tokenized argv produces nulls with no warning, surfacing as downstream TypeErrors far from the bug origin.

pitfalls.risk: Combo short flag -abc reclassifies unknown middle chars differently based on _passThroughOptions.
pitfalls.consequence: Non-deterministic-looking parse trees depending on a rarely set flag.

pitfalls.risk: _storeOptionsAsProperties (legacy) is no longer tamper-evident; setting program.foo = 42 corrupts the parsed value and lies via getOptionValueSource.
pitfalls.consequence: Buggy middleware can defeat conflict detection and env-priority logic.

pitfalls.risk: childProcess.spawn for executable subcommands uses stdio:'inherit' but never shell:true; executable name is user-controlled.
pitfalls.consequence: Path traversal only via the configured _executableDir; no shell injection vector, but executable search directory should still be validated by the consumer.

conventions: All mutators on Command return this for chaining.
Errors are CommanderError subclasses with exitCode/code/nestedError; user-facing errors include bulleted remediation hints.
Output behavior is injected via configureOutput({writeOut, writeErr, outputError, ...}); no globals.
Subcommands inherit settings via copyInheritedSettings; factory methods (createCommand, createOption, createArgument, createHelp) are extension points.

expert_domains.rationale: Help class (lib/help.js ~734 lines) owns rendering: formatHelp, visibleCommands/visibleOptions, sortSubcommands/sortOptions, padWidth, displayWidth (strips ANSI), minWidthToWrap, longestArgumentTermLength, longestCommandTermLength, longestOptionTermLength, showGlobalOptions, style hints, suggestion strings. ~22 dedicated test files. Cohesive, recurring, with its own extension surface (createHelp / configureHelp).

key_files.purpose: Help class — formatHelp, visibleCommands/visibleOptions, sort, padding/wrap, displayWidth (strips VT), showGlobalOptions, helpGroup support

key_types.name: Help
key_types.purpose: Public Help type — overridable helpWidth, sortSubcommands, sortOptions, showGlobalOptions, prepareContext, formatHelp

patterns.name: strip-color-before-measurement
patterns.description: displayWidth uses stripVTControlCharacters so ANSI escape codes do not inflate width calculations.

patterns.name: sort-subcommands-and-options
patterns.description: Optional alphabetical sort via compareOptions (short then long, localeCompare); toggled by configureHelp sortSubcommands/sortOptions.

patterns.name: suggest-similar
patterns.description: Unknown option/command errors append (Did you mean one of X, Y, Z?) computed by lib/suggestSimilar.js using optimal-string-alignment distance, only for candidates with similarity > 0.4.

pitfalls.risk: displayWidth is computed without emoji/CJK width handling.
pitfalls.consequence: Help output misaligns when subcommand descriptions or option descriptions contain wide characters.

pitfalls.risk: helpGroup headings affect visible section ordering but not sortSubcommands ordering across groups.
pitfalls.consequence: Grouped help mixes sorted and unsorted sections unless each group is independently sorted; users may report inconsistent ordering.

conventions: Help is a class with static-style methods; extension is via subclassing or configureHelp (no constructor injection).
Visible commands/options exclude _hidden items and may include placeholder for implicit help command.
Output streams flow through _outputConfiguration.writeOut and writeErr injected from the Command.
